title: Ordinary right adjoints reindex coherent colimit cocones
statement:
Use nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, right-pinched mapping spaces and colimiting cocones as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I,J$ be small ordinary categories in a fixed universe, and let $L:J\to I$ and $R:I\to J$ be ordinary functors with an adjunction $L\dashv R$, meaning bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_I(Lj,i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_J(j,Ri)$ natural in $i,j$. Let $\mathcal E$ be any quasicategory in a sufficiently large universe, $p:N(J)\to\mathcal E$ a coherent diagram, and $e\in\mathcal E$. Restriction along $N(R)$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_J e)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(p\circ N(R),\Delta_I e),$$
where $\Delta_J e$ and $\Delta_I e$ denote the constant diagrams. This is the restriction map itself and is natural in $p$ and $e$. Consequently, for any coherent cocone $a:p\to\Delta_J c$, the cocone $a$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $N(R)$ is colimiting, with the same vertex $c$. No existence of any other colimits in $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Propositions 4.1.1.7-8, printed pp. 226 and 236-238: specialize to the nerve of an ordinary right adjoint; the comma category j/R has initial object (Lj,unit_j). Fixed-vertex cocone spaces are the fibers in Proposition 4.1.1.7, expressed in the coherent comma convention of the definition node. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Write $\phi_{j,i}:\operatorname{Hom}_I(Lj,i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_J(j,Ri)$ for the given natural bijections. Set $\eta_j=\phi_{j,Lj}(1_{Lj})$ and $\epsilon_i=\phi_{Ri,i}^{-1}(1_{Ri})$. Naturality gives $\phi_{j,i}(f)=R(f)\eta_j$ and $\phi_{j,i}^{-1}(g)=\epsilon_iL(g)$, and also makes $\eta:1_J\to RL$ and $\epsilon:LR\to1_I$ natural transformations. Substituting the identity elements in these inverse formulas gives $R\epsilon_i\,\eta_{Ri}=1_{Ri}$ and $\epsilon_{Lj}\,L\eta_j=1_{Lj}$. A natural transformation is a functor from the product with $[1]$; taking its nerve gives a simplicial map from the product with $\Delta^1$, since in degree $n$ a functor $[n]\to C\times[1]$ is exactly a pair of functors into the two factors. Thus these units, counits and their triangle identities supply coherent diagrams, with no fullness assumption on $R$.

source.place: Agent argument, ordinary-adjunction preliminaries for the coherent bar foundation of proof paragraph 2

proof.text: Put $Q_J=\operatorname{Fun}(N(J),\mathcal E)$ and $Q_I=\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] these are quasicategories and their mapping spaces are Kan complexes. Denote the two right-pinched mapping spaces in the statement by $A$ and $B$, and the actual restriction map by $r:A\to B$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] their natural comparison maps to the arrow spaces $A_U=U_{Q_J}(p,\Delta_J e)$ and $B_U=U_{Q_I}(pR,\Delta_I e)$ are homotopy equivalences. Here and below $pR$ means $p\circ N(R)$, and similarly for other index composites. Restriction is a simplicial functor, so these comparison maps commute strictly with restriction in every degree. It therefore suffices to construct a homotopy inverse to restriction $r_U:A_U\to B_U$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, applied to the two functor quasicategories; closure is the existing enhanced-functor-cone-calculus statement

proof.text: We will use the following direct consequence of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], on entire parameter spaces. If $T$ is a Kan complex and $T\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to Q$ is a family of squares in a quasicategory with four fixed vertices, restrict to the triangles with ordered vertices $(00,10,11)$ and $(00,01,11)$. These give maps from $T$ to the two triangle spaces $V$ of that node. For either map $t:T\to V$, the formula for composition there gives $[\ell t]=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}[\theta t]$: its diagonal is homotopic to the composite of its two consecutive edges, as maps from $T$. The two diagonals are the same restriction to $(00,11)$. Hence the two boundary composites of the square are homotopic as maps of spaces, not just at individual vertices. We use the natural pinch equivalences to express this calculation in arrow spaces. The same formula proves compatibility with every simplicial functor: the maps $V$, $U$, $\theta$ and $\ell$ all commute with postcomposition degree by degree, and $[\theta]$ is invertible. Associativity and identity homotopies on whole mapping spaces are supplied by the same cited node.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9 and Propositions 4.6.8.11-12; two restrictions of a parametrized square and the existing composition formula

proof.text:
The unit of step 1 gives a specified transformation $p\eta:p\to pRL$ in $Q_J$. Restriction along $N(L)$ sends $\beta\in B_U$ to $\beta L:pRL\to\Delta_J e$. Precompose with $p\eta$ using the composition maps of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] (expressed in arrow spaces via step 2). This defines a map of Kan complexes up to simplicial homotopy
$$s_U:B_U\longrightarrow A_U,\qquad \beta\longmapsto(\beta L)\circ p\eta.$$
Choose any representative of this composition homotopy class; it is a map on the whole Kan complex because the composition formula uses a homotopy inverse to $\theta$, not a separate filler for each vertex. The calculation of step 3 ensures that restricting this representative gives the homotopy class of $(\beta LR)\circ p\eta R$.

source.place: Agent construction of the inverse restriction map in the coherent bar foundation of proof paragraph 2

proof.text:
For the composite $s_Ur_U$, evaluate the universal family of transformations $\alpha:p\to\Delta_J e$ on the unit: there is a simplicial map
$$N(J)\times\Delta^1_u\times\Delta^1_v\times A_U\longrightarrow\mathcal E,\qquad (j,u,v,\alpha)\longmapsto\alpha(\eta(j,u),v).$$
This notation means composition of the evaluation map with the nerve of the functor $J\times[1]\to J$ representing $\eta$; it therefore specifies the map in all degrees. By adjunction for internal functor simplicial sets it is a family of squares in $Q_J$ with corners $p,pRL,\Delta_J e,\Delta_J e$. Its boundary edges are $p\eta,\alpha RL,\alpha,1_{\Delta_J e}$. The square calculation of step 3 and unitality in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] give $(\alpha RL)\circ p\eta\simeq\alpha$ as maps $A_U\to A_U$. Since $s_Ur_U(\alpha)$ has exactly the first displayed composite, $s_Ur_U\simeq1_{A_U}$. The parameter $A_U$ retains every higher coherence simplex.

source.place: Agent proof of the first inverse homotopy: universal cocone evaluated on the ordinary unit

proof.text:
For the other composite evaluate the universal $\beta:pR\to\Delta_I e$ on $\epsilon:LR\to1_I$. The simplicial map
$$N(I)\times\Delta^1_u\times\Delta^1_v\times B_U\longrightarrow\mathcal E,\qquad(i,u,v,\beta)\longmapsto\beta(\epsilon(i,u),v)$$
is a family of squares in $Q_I$ with corners $pRLR,pR,\Delta_I e,\Delta_I e$ and boundary edges $pR\epsilon,\beta,\beta LR,1_{\Delta_I e}$. Step 3 gives $\beta LR\simeq\beta\circ pR\epsilon$ as maps from $B_U$. Thus, by associativity in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition],
$$r_Us_U(\beta)\simeq(\beta LR)\circ p\eta R\simeq\beta\circ(pR\epsilon\circ p\eta R)\simeq\beta.$$
For the last homotopy use the actual triangle identity $R\epsilon\circ\eta R=1_R$ of step 1. Its nerve supplies the triangle with edges $N(\eta R),N(R\epsilon),1_{N(R)}$; applying $p$ and the triangle composition formula identifies the bracketed composite with the identity of $pR$, and unitality finishes the calculation. This again is a homotopy on the entire $B_U$. Therefore $r_U$ has a simplicial homotopy inverse. By [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder], the natural homeomorphism $|T\times\Delta^1|\cong |T|\times[0,1]$ identifies the realized endpoint inclusions with the ordinary cylinder endpoints. Thus the two simplicial homotopies realize to continuous inverse homotopies. Apply [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to conclude that $|r_U|$ induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group, without requiring the homotopies to fix basepoints. Hence $r_U$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The strictly commuting pinch-comparison square of step 2 then makes the specified map $r$ a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Agent proof of the second inverse homotopy: universal restricted cocone evaluated on the ordinary counit and the right triangle identity

proof.text: Restriction is natural in $p$ and $e$: its defining operation is precomposition with $N(R)$, which commutes degree by degree with evaluation, restriction of parameter simplices and constant diagrams. With varying source diagrams it commutes with precomposition by a coherent transformation, and with varying vertices it commutes with postcomposition by the corresponding constant transformation; the composition compatibility follows from the $V,\theta,\ell$ formula in step 3. For higher compatibilities, an $n$-simplex of a diagram or transformation family is an evaluation map with factors $N(J)$ and $\Delta^n$ (and the arrow interval when present). Restriction replaces only the $N(J)$ factor by $N(I)$ via $N(R)$; it commutes strictly with every face and degeneracy of $\Delta^n$, with the arrow-interval restrictions, and with the constant-diagram map. Applying the triangle-space formula to these evaluation maps gives the asserted composition compatibilities on the entire parameter spaces. Finally let $a:p\to\Delta_J c$ be the specified cocone. By the dual criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], it is colimiting exactly when, for every $e$, composition gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,e)\to A$. The analogous criterion for $aR$ uses $B$. For $f:c\to e$, restriction takes $\Delta_J(f)\circ a$ to $\Delta_I(f)\circ(aR)$ up to the composition homotopy, so the second criterion map is the composite of the first with the equivalence $r:A\to B$. A map followed by an equivalence is an equivalence if and only if that map is. Hence the two specified cocones are colimiting simultaneously, with the identical vertex $c$. The argument only uses mapping spaces of the given objects and does not assume any further colimits.

lean.statement: theorem infinity_right_adjoint_reindexing {I J : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [SmallCategory J] (L : J ⥤ I) (R : I ⥤ J) (adj : L ⊣ R) (E : SSet.{max u v}) [Quasicategory E] : (∀ (p : SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.obj (nerve J) ⟶ E) (e : E _⦋0⦌), IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (excisionMappingRestriction (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R)) p (SSet.const e))) ∧ constantDiagrams (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.obj (nerve J)) E ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R))).app E = constantDiagrams (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.obj (nerve I)) E ∧ (∀ (T : SSet.{max u v}) (H : T ⟶ (ihom (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.obj (nerve J))).obj E), MonoidalClosed.uncurry (H ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R))).app E) = (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R) ▷ T) ≫ MonoidalClosed.uncurry H) ∧ (∀ (p : SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.obj (nerve J) ⟶ E) (a : (coconeCategory p) _⦋0⦌), (IsColimiting p a ↔ IsColimiting (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R) ≫ p) ((gluingCoconeRestrict (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R)) p).app _ a)) ∧ ((gluingCoconeRestrict (SSet.uliftFunctor.{v}.map (nerveMap R)) p).app _ a).1.1 = a.1.1)
lean.note: Uses the already landed canonical mapping-space and coherent cocone restriction helpers, whose owning nodes are added to stmt_deps under brief-stage2 §5.
